sentences.text: With the consent of both learned counsel for the parties, heard finally at motion stage.

2. This appeal has been filed by the claimant/appellant under Section 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the award dated 27.08.2019 passed in MACC.No.212 OF 2019 by the Member of VIIth additional MACT, Sagar District- Sagar, seeking enhancement of compensation.
3. Learned counsel for the appellants submits that income determined by Tribunal is not proper.
It should have been determined on the basis of minimum wages.
On above ground, it is urged that compensation awarded by the Tribunal be suitably enhanced.
4. Learned counsel for respondent/Insurance Company submits that compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper and no enhancement is required.
Learned counsel for the respondent/Insurance Company also submits that compensation be limited to the extent, Court fees has been paid.

With respect to above submissions, learned counsel for the respondent-Insurance has relied upon M.A.No.155 of 2019 (Manoj Kumar and Others Vs. H.D.F.C. and Others) decided on Prabhu Kurmi vs Sanjay on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178289037/
1 17.04.2023.

entities.text: M.A.No.155 of 2019 (Manoj Kumar and Others Vs. H.D.F.C. and Others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, appeal filed by the appellants be dismissed.
5. I have heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused record of the case.
6. So far as income of deceased is concerned, in the instant case, accident occurred on 25.12.2018.
Minimum wages of an unskilled labour on the date of accident were Rs.7,375/-.
As per findings recorded by the Tribunal, deceased was aged 40 years.
Hence, 25% is to be added as future prospects and multiplier of 15 is to be applied.
Further, looking to the number of dependents, one fourth is to be deducted for personal and living expenses.
Appellants No.1, 2 and 3 being husband/sons/daughter
are also entitled to receive Rs.40,000/- each for consortium.

Further,
appellants are also entitled to receive Rs.15,000/- for loss of estate and Rs.15,000/- for funeral expenses.

7. Hence, in view of above, compensation awarded by Tribunal is recalculated as under:-
 S.No. Heads   1. Monthly Income of the deceased   2. Added Future Prospects 25% 
3. Personal & Living Expenses of the deceased Rs.6,913/-
(1/4)
4.

Monthly loss of dependency Rs.6,913/-
5.

Annual loss of dependency Rs.82,956/-
7.

Total loss of dependency Rs.12,44,340/-
8. Compensation for loss of estate and funeral Rs.30,000/-
expenses

9. Compensation for loss of spousal/parental/filial Rs.1,20,000/-
consortium 10.

Total Compensation Rs.13,94,340/-
13.

Total compensation awarded by the Tribunal Rs.8,29,375/-
14.

Actual enhancement Rs.5,64,965/-
8.
Hence, compensation awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced by Rs.5,64,965/-

Prabhu Kurmi vs Sanjay on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178289037/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 9. Enhanced compensation of Rs.5,64,965/- shall carry interest at the rate awar- ded by the Tribunal.
Other findings of the Tribunal shall remain intact.
10. So far as issue of confining enhancement of compensation to the extent Court fees is paid, in this Court's opinion, in view of law laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court in Kavita Banukila & Ors.

Vs.
Santosh Kumar Vs. Santosh Ku- mar & Anr in Civil Appeal No.8053 of 2024, enhancement of compensation cannot be restricted to the extent Court fees is paid.

entities.text: Santosh Kumar Vs. Santosh Ku- mar & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, principle laid down in Manoj Kumar (Supra) does not help appellant in any way.
11. Appellants have valued their present appeal for Rs.3,00,000/- and have paid court fees accordingly.
Therefore, appellants shall be entitled to receive en- hanced amount only after payment of deficit court fees.
12. Appeal filed by the appellants is partly allowed to the extent as indicated above and disposed of accordingly.

(ACHAL KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE vai Prabhu Kurmi vs Sanjay on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178289037/
